blocks.text: Totora reed boat beside a floating Uros island — illustration

This journey takes you through places with distinct histories. In Lima, colonial mansions and archaeological sites still stand. In Cusco, Inca stonework stands alongside Spanish churches, while Machu Picchu sits among the mountains at about 2,450 metres. The road to Puno crosses high mountain passes and passes archaeological complexes. On Lake Titicaca, you will see the floating Uros islands and Taquile. In Colombia, the route takes in the gold of pre-Columbian cultures, the story of El Dorado, the salt workings of Zipaquirá and Cartagena’s fortified Old Town.

The journey moves between different civilisations and landscapes. You will spend the first 7 days in Peru, from Lima on the Pacific coast to highland Cusco, Inca stone complexes and Machu Picchu, then across the Andes to Puno for a day on Lake Titicaca. After the flight to Bogotá, the architecture and history change. In Colombia, you will discover pre-Columbian gold, the legend of El Dorado, the salt workings and Cartagena’s Spanish fortifications. Between longer sightseeing days, you will have evenings at leisure and a full free day in Cusco.
